# Micro-test design: new sentence in api-error-messages

Status: design only. Nothing has been run. Commit this file before the first scored rep.

## Question

Does "Say what went wrong and the next step the caller can take." make agents write error messages that
include a next step, where "Say what went wrong." did not (baseline: 6 of 10 runs had no next step)?

## Open items for the partner (needed before running)

1. The scenario prompts used in the old baseline run. Reusing them keeps the old-sentence arm comparable.
   I have not seen them. If they are lost, the three tasks below stand in.
2. Whether the baseline's 10 runs were on one model. I do not know, so this design re-runs the old sentence.
3. Confirm the two models and the cap below, or change them.

## Arms

| Arm | System prompt |
|---|---|
| A. control | The skill with the sentence "Say what went wrong." deleted. Nothing else changed. |
| B. old | The skill as committed (old sentence). |
| C. new | The skill with only that sentence replaced by the new one. |

Everything else in the skill text is byte-identical across arms: frontmatter, the 200-character rule, the
example, the red flags. A is needed to show whether the failure comes from the old sentence at all. B is
re-run so each model has its own baseline. If A already contains a next step in most reps, the sentence is not
the cause, and the test stops there.

## Models

Two models, chosen by me because none was named: `claude-sonnet-5-5` and `claude-haiku-5-5`. Same number of
reps on each. A wording that binds one can fail on the other.

## Reps and tasks

Target 10 reps per arm per model: 3 arms x 2 models x 10 = 60 reps. Minimum acceptable is 5 per cell; below
that, report "not enough" instead of a verdict. Rotate three tasks over the reps, the same rotation in every
cell, so task is balanced across arms (reps 1,4,7,10 get task 1; 2,5,8 task 2; 3,6,9 task 3):

1. A POST /payments request sent `currency: "usd"`. Write the error response for the 400.
2. GET /orders/ord_123 returns nothing because the order lives under another tenant. Write the 404 response.
3. POST /users with an email that already exists. Write the 409 response.

The user message gives the task only, with no mention of next steps and no mention of the skill. The skill
text is the system prompt. These tasks tempt the failure because "name the problem and stop" is a complete-
looking answer.

## Running without an API key

Each rep is a fresh `claude -p` call, one sample per call, as the reference allows ("a fresh session isolated").
Per rep:

- Run in a new empty directory outside every repository, such as `/private/tmp/mt-run/<random-id>/`.
- Pass the arm's text as the system prompt (`--system-prompt-file`), pass the model with `--model`, and run
  with no tools (`--tools ""`). Turn off user settings, memory and CLAUDE.md for the rep. The newest
  `specs/baseline/*/kit/` has the exact flags and scrub. This repo has none yet, so I will confirm the flags
  against `claude --help` before the pilot, not guess them.
- Keep this spec, the proposal and the baseline records out of reach of the rep (not in or above its directory).
  A rep that reads one is VOID.

Pilot first, one rep, before any scored rep: ask it which instruction files, memory, tools, other sessions and
user name it can see. Any answer I did not plan for means the setup leaks; fix it, then rerun the pilot. The
pilot is not scored. Record its cost; it sets the per-rep estimate.

## Rules, registered before any reply is read

For each reply, extract the `message` text (if the reply is not an error response at all, see VOID).

- PASS: the message contains a concrete next step the caller can take: a value to send, a field to change, or
  an endpoint or action to use first. Restating the rule alone ("it must be an upper-case ISO 4217 code") is
  not a next step by itself. It counts only if the message tells the caller what to do or send, such as
  "send 'USD'". The example message in the skill is therefore a FAIL as written. This matches the baseline's
  meaning of "no next step".
- FAIL: the message names the problem and no next step.
- VOID: the rep read a forbidden file, the isolation probe found a leak that rep shared, the reply is not an
  error response, or the run errored. VOID reps are rerun, not counted.

Secondary check, scored separately and never allowed to turn a FAIL into a PASS: the message is under 200
characters, and names field, value, rule in that order (when the task has a field). The new sentence might push
length over the limit, and that is a regression worth seeing.

If a reply shows a reading the rules did not foresee, keep the verdict above and report counts under both
readings.

## Blind scoring

A script assigns each reply a random id and writes sheets that hold only the id and the `message` text. No
file name, path, order or count shows the arm, model or task. The key stays in a separate file I do not open
until every sheet has a grade. Grades go in a file; then unblind.

## What counts as success

Judged per model, on the PASS rate for the next step:

- Success: arm C passes in at least 9 of 10 on both models, and arm B stays near its baseline (failures
  clearly present). The gap should be fully separated, not marginal.
- Reps that converge on the same shape are a good sign. If C's replies show many different readings of "next
  step" (some a retry hint, some a docs link), the wording is not binding. Tighten the form before adding words.
- Fail: C is not clearly above B on either model. Or C passes the next-step check but breaks the 200-character or
  field/value/rule order on more than 2 of 10 reps. Then the sentence trades one problem for another.
- If A is as good as C, the sentence is unneeded and the change has no support.

With 10 per cell, small differences are noise. Do not call a 7-of-10 against 5-of-10 result a win.

## Spend cap and stop rule

Cap: $1.20 total for this micro-test, which keeps $0.30 of the $1.50 budget in reserve. Rule: before each
batch, stop if the running total plus that batch's worst case would pass the cap. A batch is one arm on one
model. The worst case is 10 reps at the highest per-rep cost seen so far. Record each batch's cost in a table at
the bottom of this file as it completes.

Run the order so the question is answered first if money runs out: C and B on the first model, then C and B on
the second model, then A on each. If the pilot shows 60 reps will not fit under the cap, cut reps evenly across
cells (not below 5) instead of dropping a model, and say so in the report.

## Cost log

| Batch | Reps | Cost | Running total |
|---|---|---|---|
| pilot | 1 | | |
